gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I like ___ up early in summer.
gaps.explanation: With 'like' meaning enjoy, -ing is preferred: like getting up. 'Would like' takes to: I'd like to get up.

gaps.sentence: I can't stand ___ kept waiting when I have an appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't stand' takes a gerund; the passive gerund is 'being kept'.

gaps.sentence: My boss won't ___ me take Friday off.
gaps.explanation: let + object + bare infinitive: won't let me take. (allow/permit take to: allow me to take.)

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)
avoid is followed by -ing: avoid talking.

gaps.sentence: We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.
